248	6. **Selection checkbox.** Today: always visible at the row start. Target: hidden until selection mode is active or the row is hovered or focused, and placed in the 44px gutter. While visible, the selected row keeps a non-color marker.
249	7. **Row actions.** Today: bordered text chips ("Mark read", "Archive", "More") that are always in the meta region. Target: icon-only `icon-muted` glyphs that replace the date on the focused or hovered row. Accessible names and the `meta-compact` overflow disclosure logic stay.
250	8. **Date-group caption.** Today: uppercase 0.72rem with letter-spacing and a bottom rule. Target: title case, 12px `text-secondary`, a 48px block, no rule, on the content inset.
251	9. **Contact pane.** Type done (2026-11-07 typeset pass): the "Focused conversation" / "Open conversation" caption is sentence-case 12px Ash with no tracking, the name is the 16px regular Headline, the email is 12px semibold Paper White (Title), and the "Recent cached mail" label is Title. Still today: the caption exists at all, a 0.6rem pad, bordered raised chips for recent mail, and a `minmax(230px, 280px)` width. Target: no caption; name in the 16px regular headline on the tab line; email in 12px semibold on the first-row line; a "Mail" section listing recent threads at a 24px pitch (this needs data the pane does not receive yet); a footer toolbar (a natural new home for Account, Activity and Drafts); 272px wide.
252	10. **Palette deltas.** Done: `text-primary` #ece9e2 → #ffffff (typeset pass), `text-secondary` #a8a29a → #c0bcb6 (rows pass), `text-tertiary`, `icon-muted` and `unread-marker` added (header and rows passes), and the undefined `--text-muted` on coverage notes now maps to `text-secondary`. Remaining: `divider` #3b3936 → #474543 (pane separators only; today the token also borders every global button, input and drawer row, so change it with the button pass, gap 11), and `rail-well` / `rail-button` arrive with the rail (gap 2). `focus-accent` stays at the committed #bba5ed; the capture reads about #bfa1f6, which is within capture and color-profile noise.
253	11. **Global button style.** Today: every `<button>` is a raised bordered chip. Target: ghost buttons and glyphs in the browsing shell. Raised `button-utility` chips appear only inside utility drawers and recovery banners.
254	12. **Command overlay.** Today: hard-coded off-palette violets (#24212a, #17151d, #493d60, #c7a7ff, #81718f). Target: map them to `surface-raised`, `surface-contact`, `focus-fill` and `focus-accent`.
255	13. **In-flow bars.** The Selection bar, Action notice, cached-coverage note and draft-recovery banner use bordered full-width strips with mixed paddings (their text is already 12px Body since the typeset pass). Target: borderless, 12px, aligned to the content inset, and still in flow and always visible.
256	14. **Type scale and dates.** Done (2026-11-07 typeset pass). The shell type is semantic tokens on `:root`: `--type-headline` 1rem, `--type-body` 0.75rem, `--type-count` 0.6875rem, `--type-mono` 0.85rem, weights 400/600 only (`--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong`). `.app-main` sets Body as the shell default, so the rail, contact pane, notices, drawers, the reader chrome and form controls are 12px instead of an inherited 16px or ad hoc 0.8/0.85/0.9/0.95/1.1rem. Shell h2 is Headline; h3/h4 and in-panel drawer headings are Title; the reader subject is Headline at 600. Row dates follow the Label rules below and are deterministic (no default-locale dependence: the old `30 Sept 2001` vs `Sep 30, 2001` rendered-layout gate now passes under any `LANG`). Rows carry `<time datetime>` plus the full date as the title; reader message times are full dates with `datetime`. The rendered larger-text gate now expects the compact action disclosure at a 25px root font (was 23px), since the 12px rail leaves the list wider.
257	   Remaining: the command overlay keeps its own sizes (0.8/0.9/1.5rem) until gap 12; the attachment chooser's body text still inherits 16px (only its heading is on the scale); raw ISO timestamps remain in drawer and notice copy (Account "Last synced", Cached Done coverage "Last synced", Activity group times, Provider mail catalog/page/message times, Reminders due times, reader recovery snapshot) — route them through `fullDateLabel` in a polish pass, updating their tests.
258	15. **Typeface.** Superhuman ships a proprietary face. We stay on local `system-ui` (no remote fonts), so glyph widths will differ slightly. Calibrate sizes by eye on device, not by matching the font.
259	16. **Out of scope for this capture.** The native title strip (Tauri window chrome) and the reader view are not shown. The reader's type is on the shell scale (typeset pass: Headline subject at 600, 12px message chrome, full dates, Mono body), but its layout and colours keep their current tokens until a reader reference is captured.
260	
261	## 2. Colors
262	
263	One warm charcoal ramp, one violet signal, and two status hues reserved for truth-telling.
264	
265	### Primary
266	- **Dusk Lavender** (`focus-accent`): the single "you are here" signal. Used for the 4px bar on the focused row, the active message bar in the reader, focus outlines, and the highlighted command. It never fills an area and never decorates.
267	
268	### Secondary
269	- **Orchid Dot** (`unread-marker`): only for the 5px unread dot in the row gutter. It is pinker than Dusk Lavender so that unread and focus never read as the same signal.
270	
271	### Neutral
272	- **Warm Charcoal** (`surface`): the list, rail and header plane. Everything sits on it.
273	- **Deep Umber** (`surface-contact`): the contact pane and utility drawers. It is one step darker, so context reads as secondary to the list.
274	- **Lifted Charcoal** (`surface-raised`): utility chips, overlays and inputs.
275	- **Focus Stone** (`focus-fill`): the focused-row and active-message fill, and the highlighted command item.
276	- **Inkwell** (`rail-well`): the pill behind the rail's navigation glyphs.
277	- **Rail Pebble** (`rail-button`): the circular rail action button.
278	- **Paper White** (`text-primary`): sender, subject, active tab, contact name and email, labels.
279	- **Ash** (`text-secondary`): snippet, date, group caption, contact threads, counts.
280	- **Smoke** (`text-tertiary`): inactive split tabs.
281	- **Graphite** (`icon-muted`): every resting glyph (row actions, compose, search, hamburger, footer icons, attachment). Hover and focus raise glyphs to Paper White.
282	- **Seam** (`divider`): the 1px vertical separators between rail, list and contact pane. Nothing else.
283	
284	### Status
285	- **Amber Notice** (`warning`): pending, outcome unknown, local-only, expired-undo and partial states.
286	- **Coral Fault** (`danger`): confirmed failures and command errors.
287	
288	### Named Rules
289	**The One Signal Rule.** Dusk Lavender appears at most once per screen, on the current row or message. If two violet things are visible, one of them is wrong.
290	
291	**The Seams-Only Rule.** Dividers separate panes, never rows. Rows are separated by rhythm alone.
292	
293	**The Status-Is-Sacred Rule.** Amber and coral are never used decoratively, and a status is never shown only as a tint: every status carries words.
294	
295	## 3. Typography
296	
297	**Body Font:** system-ui (with -apple-system, sans-serif)
298	**Label/Mono Font:** ui-monospace, for plain-text message bodies only
299	
300	**Character:** One local system sans in two weights carries the whole UI. Hierarchy comes from weight (600 vs 400) and tone (Paper White vs Ash), not size. The browsing shell uses just two sizes.
301	
302	### Hierarchy
303	- **Headline** (400, 1rem / 16px, 1.25): split tabs and the contact name. This is the only large text in the shell.
304	- **Title** (600, 0.75rem / 12px, 1.35): sender names, contact email, section labels ("Mail"), footer labels, notice labels.
305	- **Body** (400, 0.75rem / 12px, 1.35): subject (Paper White), snippet and threads (Ash), date-group captions (Ash).
306	- **Label** (400, 0.75rem / 12px, tabular numerals): dates ("8:00 AM", "6 NOV" with an uppercase month) and counts in status text.
307	- **Mono** and the other steps are CSS tokens: `--type-headline`, `--type-body`, `--type-count`, `--type-mono`, `--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong` (`src/assets/style.css`). Use the tokens, never a literal size.
308	
309	### Dates
310	Row and reader dates are one fixed product format, not a locale format. They depend only on the instant, the current time and the viewer's time zone (`src/lib/browsing-dates.ts`). Month group captions ("October 2026") still follow the locale.
311	- **Row, today:** the time, 12-hour, no leading zero: "8:00 AM", "12:05 PM".
312	- **Row, earlier this calendar year:** day and month: "6 NOV". The DOM text is "6 Nov"; CSS uppercases it, so screen readers hear a word, not letters.
313	- **Row, any other year (past or future):** day, month and four-digit year: "9 JAN 2025". The day is kept for precision, and a two-digit year would read as another day.
314	- **Unknown or unparsable:** "Unknown" in the row, "Unknown date" in full form. Never blank.
315	- **Full form** (reader message times, the row date's hover title): "Thu 9 Jan 2025, 6:29 PM". The same 12-hour clock as the row.
316	- Every rendered date is a `<time>` with a normalized ISO `datetime` when the timestamp parses.
317	- **Count** (400, 0.6875rem / 11px): split-tab counts, set 4px after the tab label.
318	- **Mono** (400, 0.85rem, 1.45): the current plain-text message body in the reader.
319	
320	Sizes are rem so the 16px and 20px root-font layouts in `tests/inbox-list.rendered-layout.test.ts` still scale. Row and header heights are min-heights in px. The 12px row size is measured from the capture: system-ui glyph metrics point to 11.5–12px.
321	
322	### Named Rules
323	**The Two-Size Rule.** The browsing shell uses 16px and 12px only (11px for counts). A third size in the list needs a written reason.
324	
325	**The No-Caps-Caption Rule.** No uppercase letter-spaced captions in the browsing shell. Date groups and pane headings are title case. Uppercase is allowed only for the month in compact dates.
326	
327	## 4. Elevation
328	
329	The browsing shell is flat. Depth comes from tonal layering: Warm Charcoal for the plane, Deep Umber for context, Focus Stone for the current row, Inkwell for the rail well. No shadows sit on rows, panes, the header or the rail. Shadows appear only on surfaces that truly float above the shell and cover it.
330	
331	### Shadow Vocabulary
332	- **Drawer cast** (`box-shadow: -8px 0 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`): the right-edge utility drawer (Activity, Account, Drafts).
333	- **Popover lift** (`box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)`): the compact row-actions disclosure panel.
334	- **Overlay lift** (`box-shadow: 0 16px 64px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.53)`): the command palette and navigator, over a `#00000088` backdrop.
335	
336	### Named Rules
337	**The Flat-Shell Rule.** If something in the rail, header, list or contact pane casts a shadow, remove it. Shadows mean "this covers the shell", nothing else.
338	
339	## 5. Components
340	
341	### Conversation Row (signature)
342	The core of the product: dense, quiet and exact.
343	- **Shape:** square corners (0), a fixed 36px height, inset 6px from both pane edges.
344	- **Layout:** a 44px gutter (unread dot, or the checkbox in selection mode), then a 132px sender (Title, Paper White, ellipsis), then the subject (Body, Paper White) and snippet (Body, Ash) on one line with 12px gaps, then the trailing date (Label, Ash) about 25px from the pane edge. An attachment glyph (Graphite, 16px) sits before the date when present.
345	- **Focused:** Focus Stone fill plus a 4px Dusk Lavender bar on the fill's own left edge. The date gives way to three action glyphs (done, snooze, more) at a 32px pitch.
346	- **Hover:** a barely-there lift (`rgba(255,255,255,0.03)`). Action glyphs appear; focus and read state never change.
347	- **Pending / unknown:** an Amber Notice word ("Pending…") in the meta region, never just a tint.
348	- **Selected:** the visible checkbox plus a secondary inset bar, so selection never relies on color alone and never replaces the focus bar.
349	
350	### Date Group Caption
351	- **Style:** Body, Ash, title case ("Yesterday"), on the 50px content inset, in a 48px block. No rule and no background band. Not focusable.
352	
353	### Split Tabs (Navigation)
354	- **Style:** Headline type. The active tab is Paper White; inactive tabs are Smoke. The count (11px, Ash) follows 4px after the label and disappears at zero. Tabs are spaced 18px apart.
355	- **Header:** 78px tall, no bottom border. The hamburger is a Graphite glyph to the left of the inset; compose and search are Graphite glyphs on the right, at the row-action pitch.
356	
357	### Rail
358	- **Style:** 40px wide on Warm Charcoal, with a 1px Seam on its right. The top action is a 28px Rail Pebble circle aligned to the tab line. The destination glyphs sit in a 28px Inkwell pill at a 28px pitch. The active destination glyph is Paper White and the rest are Graphite.
359	- **Labels:** icon-only on screen. Every button keeps its accessible name and `title`.
360	
361	### Contact Pane
362	- **Style:** 272px on Deep Umber, with a 1px Seam on its left and a 24px inset. No caption heading.
363	- **Content:** the name in Headline on the tab line; the email in Title on the first-row line; a "Mail" section label (Title with a 16px glyph) followed by recent threads (Body, Ash, ellipsis, 24px pitch); exact known data only, never invented enrichment.
364	- **Footer:** pinned 24px from the bottom. A ghost Title label plus Graphite glyphs at a 28px pitch hold the utilities.
365	
366	### Buttons
367	- **Ghost (browsing shell):** transparent, Paper White Title text or a Graphite glyph, 4px radius, `2px 8px`. On hover or focus, the glyph rises to Paper White; the focus ring is a 2px Dusk Lavender outline at a 1px offset.
368	- **Utility (drawers, recovery banners):** a Lifted Charcoal fill with a 1px Seam border, 4px radius, `2px 8px`. This is the only bordered button.
369	
370	### Command Overlay
371	- **Style:** a Lifted Charcoal panel, 10px radius, 576px max width, Overlay lift, 15vh from the top. The input sits on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border. The highlighted item gets a Focus Stone fill plus a 3px Dusk Lavender left bar. Shortcuts are shown as `kbd` in Ash.
372	
373	### Inputs / Fields
374	- **Style:** a Lifted Charcoal fill, a 1px Seam border, 4px radius, inherited font.
375	- **Focus:** the border shifts to Dusk Lavender. No glow.
376	
377	### In-flow Notices (Action notice, Selection bar, coverage and recovery)
378	- **Style:** borderless strips in normal flow above the list, aligned to the 50px content inset, in Body type. Status words use Amber Notice or Coral Fault. Undo shows its `kbd` hint in Ash. They never overlay rows and never auto-hide a failure.
379	
380	## 6. Do's and Don'ts
381	
382	### Do:
383	- **Do** keep rows at exactly 36px with 12px type, and separate them by rhythm alone.
384	- **Do** align split tabs, sender names, date captions and notices to the single 50px content inset.
385	- **Do** use Dusk Lavender (#bba5ed) only for the current row or message, and the focus ring.
386	- **Do** show every pending, partial, failed and outcome-unknown state in words, in Amber Notice or Coral Fault, where the user is already looking.
387	- **Do** align the contact pane to the list: the name on the tab line, the email on the first-row line.
388	- **Do** ship glyphs as local inline SVG with an accessible name. No icon fonts and no CDN.
389	- **Do** treat Superhuman's browsing look as the visual and interaction reference. Close look parity is the goal (PRODUCT.md).
390	
391	### Don't:
392	- **Don't** draw dividers between rows or under the header. Seams separate panes only.
393	- **Don't** use uppercase letter-spaced captions in the browsing shell.
394	- **Don't** add Gmail-web clutter: toolbars of rarely-used icons, or chrome competing with content.
395	- **Don't** add "AI magic" chrome: sparkle icons, or generated summaries presented as fact.
396	- **Don't** build a Superhuman feature-parity clone. Copy the browsing look, not Superhuman's product scope.
397	- **Don't** use generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics: card grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration.
398	- **Don't** show optimistic UI that lies: no "Done" toast before the provider confirms, and no silent retry of an ambiguous send.
399	- **Don't** put shadows on anything in the rail, header, list or contact pane.
400	- **Don't** introduce a third type size in the list, or use off-palette hex values (the old command-overlay violets are the cautionary example).
401	- **Don't** load remote fonts, images or CDN assets.

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Gmail mailbox shell: compact browsing shell (UX-01), plain-text reader,
 * operation recovery, and explicit account/action capability gates.
 *
 * Account gate: the account status read decides fixture-vs-Gmail. While the status
 * is loading or failed, the UI renders no mailbox content at all — it never falls
 * back silently to fixture mode.
 *
 * Layout contract: a persistent narrow email rail, a 78px split header in the
 * list column (no status line), one central surface that is either the list or the
 * reader (never both), and contact context. Account/Activity/Drafts live in
 * explicit labelled utility disclosures instead of permanent competing columns;
 * the contact pane shows only exact known fields.
 *
 * Keyboard contract (window-level, one handler):
 * - j / ArrowDown, k / ArrowUp: move conversation focus in the list (row focus
 *   follows). Inside the reader only j/k switch conversations; ArrowUp/Down
 *   keep native scrolling there.
 * - Enter: open the focused conversation. Escape: close the active utility or
 *   contact disclosure first, then the reader.
 * - e: archive the focused (or reader-open) conversation when actions are enabled.
 * - Shift+E: restore to Inbox; G then E (within 1000ms): cached Done.
 * - Left from list navigation: destination navigator; pointer Commands opens palette.
 * - Cmd+K opens the palette in native mode only (browser reservations stay native).
 * - Shift+U: explicitly mark the focused/open conversation unread.
 * - z: undo the last accepted conversation action (single level, 10 s window;
 *   the backend's eligibility decision is authoritative). Cmd/Ctrl+Z is left
 *   to native text editing.
 * - Ignored with Ctrl/Meta/Alt held, during IME composition, inside text fields, and
 *   Enter/e are ignored when a button owns the key (it activates itself).
 * - While a visible draft editor exists, every mailbox shortcut is suppressed;
 *   a suspended editor behind another disclosure must not own keys. While a
 *   utility/contact disclosure is open, Escape closes it and mailbox shortcuts
 *   underneath are suppressed. Draft text has no submit/send path and is
 *   rendered only as ordinary text.
 */
import { computed, nextTick, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import CachedTrashPanel from './components/CachedTrashPanel.vue';
import { emptyCachedTrash } from './lib/cached-trash';
import ActionOverlay from './components/ActionOverlay.vue';
import RemindersPanel from './components/RemindersPanel.vue';
import ActionNotice, { type GroupNoticeView } from './components/ActionNotice.vue';
import SelectionBar from './components/SelectionBar.vue';
import HeaderGlyph from './components/HeaderGlyph.vue';
import { browsingActions, actionLabel, type BrowsingActionId } from './lib/browsing-actions';
import InboxList from './components/InboxList.vue';
import SplitEditor from './components/SplitEditor.vue';
import { splitBadge } from './lib/saved-split';
import type { SavedSplit } from './lib/ipc/client';
import ReaderView from './components/ReaderView.vue';
import AttachmentChooser from './components/AttachmentChooser.vue';
import ActivityPanel from './components/ActivityPanel.vue';
import AccountPanel from './components/AccountPanel.vue';
import DraftsPanel from './components/DraftsPanel.vue';
import ProviderDestinations from './components/ProviderDestinations.vue';
import ContactPane from './components/ContactPane.vue';
import { BROWSER_PREVIEW_DISCLOSURE } from './lib/ipc/browser-fake';
import type { ClientMode } from './lib/ipc';
import type { ConversationRef, DraftRef, DraftSource, MailClient } from './lib/ipc/client';
let nowTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;

/**
 * Single-slot notice state, single-or-group identity (UX-04/UX-05). Status text
 * derives from the matching Activity row / authoritative group status on every
 * refresh; undo windows come only from refreshed authoritative state. The
 * backend stays the authority: an `expired` rejection refreshes and then closes
 * the slot window below. After a successful undo the slot reports the outcome.
 */
const actionNotice = computed(() => {
  const groupSlot = mailbox.lastGroup.value;
  if (groupSlot) {
    const status = groupSlot.status;
    const counts = { pending: 0, confirmed: 0, failed: 0, rejected: 0, unknown: 0, cancelled: 0 };
    if (status) {
      for (const member of status.members) {
        if (member.status === 'rejected') counts.rejected += 1;
        else if (member.status === 'confirmed') counts.confirmed += 1;
        else if (member.status === 'failed') counts.failed += 1;
        else if (member.status === 'outcome_unknown') counts.unknown += 1;
        else if (member.status === 'cancelled') counts.cancelled += 1;
        else counts.pending += 1; // queued | applying
      }
    }
    let undoneView: GroupNoticeView['undone'] = null;
    const undoMembers = status?.undoReceipt?.members ?? groupSlot.undone?.members;
    if (undoMembers) {
      const skipReasons: Record<string, number> = {};
      let cancelled = 0;
      let compensating = 0;
      let skipped = 0;
      for (const member of undoMembers) {
        if (member.decision.kind === 'cancelled') cancelled += 1;
        else if (member.decision.kind === 'compensating') compensating += 1;
        else {
          skipped += 1;
          skipReasons[member.decision.reason] = (skipReasons[member.decision.reason] ?? 0) + 1;
        }
      }
      // CURRENT compensation outcomes: prefer the backend's persisted undo
      // record (also correct after restart / lost undo response); fall back to
      // the refreshed activity rows for compensations it lists. Compensation
      // status is tracked separately from the original execution statuses.
      const outcomes = { confirmed: 0, failed: 0, unknown: 0, pending: 0 };
      const record = groupSlot.status?.undoReceipt;
      if (record) {
        for (const member of record.members) {
          for (const compensation of member.compensations) {
            if (compensation.status === 'confirmed') outcomes.confirmed += 1;
            else if (compensation.status === 'failed') outcomes.failed += 1;
            else if (compensation.status === 'outcome_unknown') outcomes.unknown += 1;
            else outcomes.pending += 1;
          }
        }
      } else {
        for (const member of groupSlot.undone?.members ?? []) {
          for (const operationId of member.operationIds) {
            const row = mailbox.activity.value.find((item) => item.id === operationId);
            if (!row) outcomes.pending += 1;
            else if (row.status === 'confirmed') outcomes.confirmed += 1;
            else if (row.status === 'failed') outcomes.failed += 1;
            else if (row.status === 'outcome_unknown') outcomes.unknown += 1;
            else outcomes.pending += 1;
          }
        }
      }
      undoneView = { cancelled, compensating, skipped, skipReasons, compensationOutcomes: outcomes };
    }
    const group: GroupNoticeView = {
      count: groupSlot.members.length,
      counts,
      acceptanceUnknown: groupSlot.state === 'acceptance-unknown',
      statusKnown: status !== null,
      statusError: groupSlot.statusError,
      undoableUntil: status?.undo.undoableUntil ?? null,
      hadWindow: groupSlot.hadWindow,
      undone: undoneView,
    };
    const groupActionId: LastActionId = groupSlot.kind === 'star' ? (groupSlot.requestedStarred ? 'star' : 'unstar') : groupSlot.kind === 'read'
      ? (groupSlot.requestedRead ? 'read' : 'unread')
      : (groupSlot.requestedArchived ? 'archive' : 'unarchive');

# UX-01 — Compact browsing shell: implemented contract and evidence

Status: implemented at the component/composable/core-contract level and validated
with the repository's automated gates. Targeted real-Chrome checks of the
synthetic browser preview also pass for contact resize/focus, Inbox/Activity
navigation, and a nonzero-scroll reader round trip. Native fixture/WKWebView,
full visual calibration, and assistive-technology verification remain
**explicitly pending**. These targeted browser probes do not establish native
E2E correctness or Superhuman equivalence.

Grounding: `docs/superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md` (UX-01, acceptance
BROWSE-01, BROWSE-05 conversation portion, BROWSE-17, BROWSE-20) and
`superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md` (main-list composition, visual tokens,
reconstruction layout policy, reader replacement, contact context).

## Bounded UX-01 contract

What shipped:

- A persistent narrow email rail (Inbox + utility entries), a compact Inbox
  navigation/status header (count, pending operations, last-command error,
  preview disclosure), one central surface that is either the conversation list
  or the reader — never both at once — and a contact-context surface.
- Compact one-line rows: constrained sender, single-line subject/snippet,
  trailing compact date and row-scoped actions, ~36px scanning rhythm, lavender
  focus bar on a soft warm-gray fill, low-contrast warm dividers, and unused
  space below short lists (rows are not stretched). The subject keeps a
  readable floor (its column ≥ 136px, ~104px of subject text at the default
  font). If larger text and metadata exhaust the available row width,
  actions move behind a measured, named “More actions” disclosure; pending,
  read-state, and date remain on the row. Regression coverage includes the
  1000px contact breakpoint with 16px and 20px root fonts and an older date.
  Compact metadata presentation keeps full accessible names: visible
  "Unknown"/"Read"/"Unread" state with `aria-label="Read state unknown"`, and
  compact row action chips whose labels carry the complete "Mark read" /
  "Mark unread" semantics via `aria-label`.
- Non-selectable chronological date group headings derived in the viewer's
  calendar; they never reorder the backend's rows and are never actionable or
  tabbable.
- Account/Activity/Drafts moved into explicit labelled utility disclosures with
  keyboard-operable entry/close controls, Escape precedence, and focus
  restoration. The drafts editor routes to the drafts disclosure; close
  protection and draft recovery states remain visible or one click away; every
  user departure from an active drafts drawer (Close, another utility,
  Contact, Inbox) goes through the protected flush-and-close lifecycle and
  keeps the exact editor buffer visible on failure instead of leaving a hidden
  editor owning the keyboard. Utility and contact disclosures are mutually
  exclusive, and draft save or close failures remain recoverable even when the
  drafts drawer is not the visible surface.

Explicitly out of scope (unchanged from the plan's non-goals): message-level
focus/expansion (UX-02), bulk selection, Undo, command palette, search, saved
splits, labels/stars/reminders, native tabs, multi-account infrastructure, any
AI or calendar control, and no empty reserved regions for them (BROWSE-20).

## Supervisor-approved decisions recorded here

- **Strict 1000 CSS px contact breakpoint.** At `>= 1000px` the contact pane is
  a persistent column; strictly below `1000px` it is replaced by a
  keyboard-operable Contact disclosure. When the viewport shrinks across the
  breakpoint while the contact content holds focus, focus returns to the
  disclosure control so focus never lands in hidden content.
- **Local-calendar bucket precedence.** `Today`, `Yesterday`,
  `Earlier this month`, one named month+year bucket per calendar month, and an
  explicit `Unknown date` bucket for missing/unparsable timestamps. Bucketing
  uses the viewer's calendar (optional explicit IANA zone, otherwise the
  environment zone), computed on wall-clock components so Yesterday correctly
  crosses month, year, and DST boundaries. Backend row order is preserved; a
  heading is emitted only where the bucket changes between consecutive rows.
- **Exact newest-From semantics for the primary correspondent.**
  `ConversationSummary.primaryCorrespondent` is derived only from
  `messages.last().from` of the ordered detail stack in both summary builders
  (fixture `store.rs` and `gmail/store.rs`); it is never guessed from the
  unordered participant list, never fabricated, and nullable display names pass
  through unchanged. The field is additive: absent values are omitted on the
  wire (`skip_serializing_if`, `ts(optional)`), legacy summaries without the
  field still deserialize, and the TypeScript contract is regenerated only via
  `mise run gen:ts` (never hand-edited). The browser fake mirrors the exact
  behavior, including self-authored latest messages.
- **Focus is not selection.** Rows use ordinary `list`/`listitem` semantics with
  Against the pre-fix layout the same test fails (subject column 0px),
  demonstrating red/green. The parent independently confirmed both results:
  green on the working tree and red in an isolated copy with only the pre-fix

  UI run reported 199 passed and this one browser test skipped, followed by the

## Follow-up P1 fixes: covered actions and larger text

- **Covered actions.** The central list/reader surface is `inert` while a
  utility drawer or the narrow Contact disclosure is open. Rail and active
  disclosure controls remain available; closing the disclosure restores
  central interaction. This prevents Tab/Shift+Tab from reaching covered mail
  actions and Enter from activating them behind a drawer.
- **Larger text.** A row-local `ResizeObserver` detects when inline actions no
  longer fit. Compact rows offer a named “More actions” disclosure containing
  the same explicit read/unread/archive controls and stable IDs. Its local
  Escape handling returns focus to the toggle; a panel near the list bottom
  opens upward. This fixes the reproduced 1000px/20px-root-font overflow with
  unknown read facts, pending membership, and an old date without shrinking
  the user's root font or clipping actions.

  old-date, unknown-plus-pending cases and operable compact actions. These
  tests use isolated synthetic previews and caller-supplied Chrome, not real
  accounts or native IPC.

Now I'm working out the layout for the contact pane's identity block. The name needs to sit centered at 42px from the top, so I'm planning a header row of fixed height with the name vertically centered in it, and the email on a shorter row beneath.

I'm weighing how to keep the copy buttons reachable without leaving a blank line under the name and email. Reserving a narrow right-hand slot inside each row seems better than absolute positioning, since it avoids covering long names and doesn't add any vertical space.

I'm weighing a long name that wraps onto two lines against the alignment of a single tab line, and leaning toward a single-line ellipsis with the full name kept in the title attribute. I'll keep the copy controls as small trailing glyph buttons, each with visually hidden "Copy name" or "Copy email" text, so the vertical gaps go away.

I'm settling the name row so it stays centered on the tab line: a 72px block with the name vertically centered and 6px of top padding. A two-line name still centers around the same point, so only very long names push past that block. The email row gets a 36px block, also centered, which puts it at the expected position below.

I'm handling the unknown-contact case by putting "No correspondent information is available." on the name line, in the small Ash text, so it sits on the tab line too. Then the "Recent cached mail" label gets a 36px row starting where the email row ends, which should center it at about 132px. The thread rows after it are on a 24px pitch, so the first one lands about 25px below the label.

I'm settling the label row at 30px so its text sits near the 131px reference, which puts the first thread row about 12px lower than the reference center rather than 25px.

Now I'm laying out the "Recent cached mail" heading: keeping that text, with an aria-hidden 16px envelope glyph placed before it inside the heading. Next I'm setting the thread items as full-width text buttons with single-line ellipsis, 24px tall, no border or background, and the full subject kept in the title attribute.

I'm going to keep the copy status message where it is, after the recent list, so that moving it doesn't shift the Mail section. I'm also noting that in the narrow drawer version the 78px name block won't line up with anything, since the drawer starts lower on the page.

I'm sizing the contact column at 272px with a grid of `auto minmax(0,1fr) 272px`, which should leave a list of about 688px at a 1000px viewport. The aligned row metrics only apply inside `.contact-column`, so the drawer version keeps its compact layout.

I'm sketching out the rail next: an inbox button at the top, a well of starred, done, destinations and trash items, a spacer, then the utilities for account, activity, drafts and contact.

I'm working through the rail's tooltip styling next: the labels stay hidden until hover or keyboard focus, then appear to the right of each button as a small raised popover, with the button itself positioned relatively to anchor it.

I'm weighing whether to add native title attributes alongside the CSS tooltip, since showing both at once would overlap. I'm leaning toward keeping the tooltip label as the accessible name and not nesting a shortcut hint inside it, so the name doesn't change.

I'm weighing whether to keep a native title tooltip on the rail buttons, since showing it alongside the CSS label would overlap on hover. I'm leaning toward dropping the title and relying on the CSS tooltip, while the shortcut hint can live in aria-keyshortcuts so the accessible name stays the same.

I'm weighing whether a CSS tooltip can carry the shortcut hint, since native titles lag by a second or so and icon-only buttons need quicker labels. The problem is that generated content inside the button might change its accessible name, so I'm leaning toward keeping the shortcut out of the name entirely.

I'm weighing whether to keep a native title on the rail buttons, since it matches the header glyphs but would double up with a CSS tooltip on hover. I'm leaning toward keeping the title for hover and showing the CSS label only on keyboard focus, because native titles never appear on focus.

I'm settling on a title attribute for every rail button, so hovering gives the full sentence like the header glyphs do. For keyboard users, I'll also show the CSS label as a tooltip on focus-visible, since native titles never appear on focus.

Now I'm working out the badge for the Activity glyph: a small count pill at the top-right, with the pending and outcome-unknown numbers split out so the screen reader text stays precise.

I'm weighing whether the badge should count unknown outcomes alongside pending ones, since the old status line did. I'm leaning toward a single visible number with a hidden description that spells out the pending and unknown counts.

I'm checking the rail's z-index so the tooltip sits above the central pane but still below an open drawer, since the tooltip lives in the rail while the list is a sibling.

I'm now thinking about the glyph component for the rail, weighing whether to make one shared icon file for the rail and the contact pane or split them, and considering whether the mail and copy glyphs belong with the rest.

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Local inline 16px glyphs for the side panes: the icon rail (destinations and
 * utilities) and the contact pane (section label, copy controls). Sibling of
 * HeaderGlyph and RowGlyph: no icon font, no CDN. Purely decorative: every
 * glyph is aria-hidden and its control carries the accessible name in text.
 */
defineProps<{
  name: 'inbox' | 'done' | 'provider' | 'trash' | 'account' | 'activity' | 'drafts' | 'contact' | 'mail' | 'copy';
}>();
</script>

<template>
  <svg
    class="pane-glyph"
    width="16"
    height="16"
    viewBox="0 0 16 16"
    fill="none"
    stroke="currentColor"
    stroke-width="1.4"
    stroke-linecap="round"
    stroke-linejoin="round"
    aria-hidden="true"
    focusable="false"
  >
    <!-- Inbox: an in-tray. -->
    <template v-if="name === 'inbox'">
      <path d="M2.5 9.25V12a1 1 0 001 1h9a1 1 0 001-1V9.25L11.6 3.8a1 1 0 00-.94-.55H5.34a1 1 0 00-.94.55z" />
      <path d="M2.5 9.25h3l.9 1.75h3.2l.9-1.75h3" />
    </template>
    <!-- Cached Done: the same check as the row Done action. -->
    <path v-else-if="name === 'done'" d="M3.25 8.5l3.1 3.1 6.4-7.2" />
    <!-- Provider mail (labels and folders, read only): a folder. -->
    <path v-else-if="name === 'provider'" d="M2.5 4.25a1 1 0 011-1h2.65l1.4 1.5h4.95a1 1 0 011 1V12a1 1 0 01-1 1h-9a1 1 0 01-1-1z" />
    <!-- Cached Trash: a bin. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'trash'">
      <path d="M2.75 4.5h10.5M6.25 4.5V3h3.5v1.5" />
      <path d="M4.25 4.5l.6 8.1a1 1 0 001 .9h4.3a1 1 0 001-.9l.6-8.1" />
      <path d="M6.75 7v3.75M9.25 7v3.75" />
    </template>
    <!-- Account: a person in a circle. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'account'">
      <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="5.75" />
      <circle cx="8" cy="6.6" r="1.9" />
      <path d="M4.35 12.35a4.25 4.25 0 017.3 0" />
    </template>
    <!-- Activity (operation outcomes): a pulse line. -->
    <path v-else-if="name === 'activity'" d="M1.75 8.25h2.6l1.65-4 3.5 8 1.6-4h3.15" />
    <!-- Local drafts: a pencil. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'drafts'">
      <path d="M10.6 2.9l2.5 2.5-6.9 6.9-3.2.75.75-3.2z" />
      <path d="M9.1 4.4l2.5 2.5" />
    </template>
    <!-- Contact disclosure (narrow viewports): a contact card. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'contact'">
      <rect x="2.25" y="3.5" width="11.5" height="9" rx="1" />
      <circle cx="6" cy="7.1" r="1.35" />
      <path d="M3.95 10.6a2.25 2.25 0 014.1 0M9.75 6.75h2M9.75 9h2" />
    </template>
    <!-- Mail section label in the contact pane: an envelope. -->
    <template v-else-if="name === 'mail'">
      <rect x="2.25" y="3.75" width="11.5" height="8.5" rx="1" />
      <path d="M2.75 4.5L8 8.4l5.25-3.9" />
    </template>
    <!-- Copy: two overlapping sheets. -->
    <template v-else>
      <rect x="5.5" y="5.5" width="7.75" height="7.75" rx="1.25" />
      <path d="M3.75 10.5h-.25a.75.75 0 01-.75-.75V3.5a.75.75 0 01.75-.75h6.25a.75.75 0 01.75.75v.25" />
    </template>
  </svg>
</template>

216:12. **Command overlay.** Today: hard-coded off-palette violets (#24212a, #17151d, #493d60, #c7a7ff, #81718f). Target: map them to `surface-raised`, `surface-contact`, `focus-fill` and `focus-accent`.

content.text:
The rail and contact pane now match the reference geometry, and every gate passes. One thing went beyond the brief's scope: I made a small fix in `InboxList.vue`, explained below. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Gates**
- `pnpm typecheck`: clean.
- `pnpm test`: 643 passed, 32 skipped, 0 failed (baseline was 639 / 32; I added 4 tests).
- Opt-in Chrome suites, run one at a time with the local Playwright Chromium: 32/32 pass (layout 2/2, disclosure-focus 1/1, reader 13/13, discovery 16/16).
- During one earlier run, the reader test "archives with action-time neighbor ordering after a mid-reading list reorder" hit its 5s timeout while vite and Chrome were also running. It passed twice in isolation on both HEAD and this tree, then passed in the full run, so it's a load-timing flake.

**The row overflow you asked me to investigate**
- **Cause:** my change exposed an existing gap in `InboxList`'s collapse logic. It only re-checks a row when the row's box changes size. At HEAD the old rail was sized in rem, so bigger text resized the list and the check ran. With the fixed 40px rail and 272px pane, bigger text no longer resizes the row, so the check never ran. Rows overflowed from a 32px root font without collapsing their actions.
- **Pre-existing part:** in a temporary HEAD worktree (now removed), compact rows also overflow from a 28px root font. That capacity limit is not mine.
- **Fix:** `InboxList` now also watches each row's sender label, whose height changes with text size. Collapse now engages at about 33px with no overflow. The compact limit has moved out to about 35.5px.
- **Test change:** I moved the larger-text gate's checkpoints from 16/20/25px to 16/30/34.5px. Every assertion is unchanged.

**Before → after**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rail width | 5rem text column, grew with font (~93px at 16px root) | 40px fixed |
| Contact width | 230–280px | 272px fixed |
| Contact padding | 0.6rem | 0 24px 24px |
| Contact name | below a caption | centred 42px down, same line as the "Inbox" tab |
| Contact email | separated by an invisible "Copy name" line | centred 96px down, the first list line |
| Recent mail | bordered chips | label at 129px, rows at 156 / 180 / 204 / 228 (24px pitch) |

On the rail, the top circle and the tab line are both centred 42px down, and the first glyph in the dark pill is centred at 96px. These numbers hold at both 1030 and 1280px wide.

**Where each rail item went**
- **Top circle:** Inbox. There's no AI or compose action to put there, and Inbox is better than an empty or dead control.
- **Dark pill:** Starred (Gmail only), Cached Done, Provider mail, Cached Trash (Gmail only).
- **Bottom:** Account (Gmail only), Activity, Drafts, and Contact below 1000px.
- **Unchanged:** every button keeps its visible-label text as its accessible name (now visually hidden), plus `aria-current` / `aria-expanded`, its `data-test` and its handlers. Every button has a hover `title`, and a label tooltip appears beside it on keyboard focus.
- **Glyphs:** new local SVGs in `PaneGlyph.vue`; Starred reuses the header's star.

**Contact pane**
- **Caption:** "Focused/Open conversation" is still there for screen readers but hidden on screen.
- **Copy buttons:** each is a glyph at the end of its own line, shown on hover or focus and always reachable by keyboard. Hidden buttons no longer leave empty lines. Without a display name, Copy email sits on the name line.
- **Recent mail:** plain one-line text buttons with an ellipsis and the full subject as the title.
- **No footer:** the contact column doesn't exist below 1000px and is inert while a drawer is open. Utilities there would vanish on narrow windows and couldn't close their own drawer, so they live only in the rail.

**Pending badge**
- **Count:** queued + applying + outcome unknown, taken from the same rows the Activity drawer lists. There's no new IPC, and the badge shows "99+" past 99.
- **Visible digit:** amber and hidden from screen readers.
- **Words:** read out as the button's description and added to its title, e.g. "2 operations pending" or "3 operations unresolved: 2 pending, 1 outcome unknown".
- **At zero:** it disappears.
- **Limit:** it counts only what the Activity snapshot carries, not a mailbox-wide total.
